component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007): duplexes and single-family attached houses (made consistent with duplexes) in residential districts, residential infill and district-intensity changes, flag lots with narrower poles, the Small House/Small Lot option restructured as a small-lot bonus
coverage: City of Durham: residential districts in the urban tier, and RU-5 and RU-5(2) in the suburban tier
coding_notes: City Council approved 6-1 on 2019-09-03. Effective date not stated on the city page and the ordinance (Attachment B) could not be opened (Durham DocumentCenter returns 403; durham.municipal.codes is offline): effective_date is coded as the vote date. Case TC1800007 (one city notice says TC1800005, apparently a typo). Planning Commission 12-1 on 2019-06-11. unit_cap=2 reads the duplex as the largest new housing type on a single lot (the ordinance text was not read). The city page says ADUs are not permitted with duplexes or the 2,000 sq ft Small Lot Bonus Option; the small-lot minimum itself was not read in the ordinance, so min_lot_sqft is left empty. by_right, owner_occ, lot_split and parking not sourced. coverage_zones left empty: the urban-tier district list is a map layer, not a list. Second coder (Codex, 2026-11-01): partly. Current live code says “No additional parking is required”; individual ADU max 1,000 sf single story / 1,200 heated sf total in relevant civic provisions; EHC is limited geography except 800-sf cap countywide according to city page.

component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007) adopted by the Durham County Board of Commissioners for the unincorporated county (joint Durham UDO)
coverage: Unincorporated Durham County: residential districts in the urban tier and RU-5/RU-5(2) in the suburban tier
coding_notes: Board of County Commissioners approved 5-0 at a rescheduled hearing on 2019-10-28 (city EHC page). Effective date not found: coded as the vote date. Official page: “Most provisions” limited to urban residential / RU-5 tiers; some, including 800 sq ft allowance, county-wide.

component: Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD, TC2200001): minimum off-street parking requirements eliminated citywide for new development
parking: No minimum parking requirements
coverage: City of Durham, citywide
coding_notes: Council vote 'minutes to midnight on Monday, November 20, 2023' (Strong Towns, 2023-11-21). The round-3 brief lists 2023-11-21 (the day it was reported); coded 2023-11-20. Second coder (Codex, 2026-11-01): yes. UDO amendment history: TC22-01 Simplify Codes for Affordable Development, effective 1/1/2024. City Council approved 11/20/2023; County approved 12/11/2023.

component: TC-5-20, Ord. (2021) 263 TC 451 (Missing Middle): attached houses (duplexes) in R-2 and R-4, townhouses in R-6 (and in R-2 in compact, conservation or cottage-court developments), apartments in R-10 on smaller lots; units-per-acre limits removed in every residential district except R-1; one ADU per lot regardless of density
coverage: City of Raleigh residential districts R-2, R-4, R-6 and R-10 (R-1 keeps its density limit)
coding_notes: Ordinance states 'Adopted: July 6, 2021' and 'Effective: August 5, 2021' (Sec. 43: 30 days after adoption). Lot size and area per unit now control yield (minimum lot area R-1 40,000, R-2 20,000, R-4 10,000, R-6 6,000 sq ft; lot-area-per-unit rows of 2,500/2,000/1,500 sq ft not mapped to districts), so unit_cap and min_lot_sqft stay empty. Parking: only parking setbacks changed. by_right and lot_split not coded (the ordinance lists permitted building types; review path not read). Second coder (Codex, 2026-11-01): partly. Partly: 2021 TC-5-20 permits two-family homes in all districts except R-1 under single-family standards; the exact three-/four-unit pathways require use-table verification.

component: TC-20-21, Ord. (2022) 362 TC 466 (Missing Middle 2.0): tiny houses (≤800 sq ft footprint, ≤1,200 sq ft floor area) as one or two units with smaller minimum lots, flag lots for tiny houses, two-unit townhouses in R-4, ADUs on townhouse lots, a Frequent Transit Development Option (20% of units beyond 12 affordable at 60% AMI for 30 years)
coverage: City of Raleigh residential districts; the development option in Frequent Transit Areas
coding_notes: Ordinance states 'Adopted: May 10, 2022' and 'Effective: August 8, 2022' (Sec. 41: 90 days after adoption); the city FAQ agrees. Tiny-house minimum lot area: R-1 40,000, R-2 15,000, R-4 7,500, R-6 3,000 (from 4,500), R-10 2,000 (from 3,000) sq ft as read from the redline (strike-through extraction ambiguous for R-6 and R-10), so min_lot_sqft stays empty. lot_split=True reads the new flag lots for tiny houses as allowing new small lots. Approval is administrative per the FAQ; by_right not coded. Second coder (Codex, 2026-11-01): partly. Partly: TC-20-21 adopted May 10, 2022 and effective August 8, 2022; exact affected districts and unit types are not established by the adoption-date evidence alone.

component: Unified Development Ordinance: duplexes and triplexes allowed on lots in the Neighborhood 1 (N1) districts that replaced the single-family districts (R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-8 → N1-A to N1-D; UR-1 → N1-E)
coverage: City of Charlotte, Neighborhood 1 districts (conventional districts only; conditional districts keep their legacy rules)
coding_notes: Adopted 6-4 on 2022-08-22, effective 2023-06-01 (Charlotte Regional Business Alliance); the city's UDO page is behind bot protection and was not opened. The translation of legacy districts is UDO Table 3-1 (text amendment 2023-174, p. 49). Triplex conditions in the 2022 text (e.g. lot or corner requirements) and N1 parking minimums were not read: by_right, min_lot_sqft and parking stay empty. In March 2024 staff proposed limiting triplexes to corner lots in N1-A to N1-D (Charlotte Ledger, WFAE); text amendment 2024-067 (reported decided 2024-06-24) was not opened, so no superseding row yet. V5 holdout reform: Charlotte outcomes from 2023-06-01 are hidden. Second coder (Codex, 2026-11-01): partly. Partly: current UDO allows duplexes/triplexes on N1 single-family lots; quadplexes require the applicable Article 15 approval pathway. The historical 2023 row should be understood as the UDO effective date, not a separate later reform.

component: S.L. 2026-59 (S445, Regulatory Reform Act of 2026) Sec. 44, new G.S. 160D-917: at least one ADU per single-family detached house in residential zones; no conditional zoning, no parking minimums, no ban on renting house and ADU separately long-term, fees no higher than for a single-family house; local size cap must be 800-1,000 sq ft; no separate subdivision
parking: No minimum parking or parking restrictions
coverage: Charlotte: single-family detached houses in areas zoned residential; not in historic preservation districts or National Historic Landmarks; private covenants unaffected
coding_notes: S.L. 2026-59 (S445) Sec. 44, new G.S. 160D-917, applied to Charlotte only: the law covers non-coastal cities of 50,000 or more (2020 Census and 2025 estimate both at or above 50,000). Ratified 2026-08-06, signed 2026-08-11, effective 2027-01-15 for ADU permit applications on or after that date; local rules due 2027-07-01. by_right inferred from the mandate and the ban on conditional zoning; adu_max_sqft=800 is the smallest cap a city may set (up to 1,000). Replaces the statewide row NC-37-adu-2027 (a 2-digit row would apply to every NC place). The city's own ADU rule is coded in its own rows; the scenario counts the more permissive.
